Subject: RFP: regional service continuity clarifications

Jonas,

Thanks for the RFP answer set — a few follow-ups from our DR working group as we map acceptance criteria into our procurement review. We need specifics to slot Redwood into our table of vendor commitments. Can you confirm the following with as much precision and evidence as possible?

1) RTO commitments by deployment type (Hosted API, Dedicated Reserved, Private/VPC). Please indicate whether the time is for automated failover or recovery with engineering intervention.
2) RPO expectations for: model artifacts, customer data (examples: embeddings, conversations stored in customer projects), and inference runtime state (KV cache/in-flight contexts).
3) Typical failover sequencing (DNS vs BGP vs traffic-proxy), expected TTLs, and whether you support incremental/canary routing for gradual cutover.
4) How data durability is assured across regions (replication approach, A/A or A/P, replication lag targets).
5) Test cadence and evidence — we will want a recent rehearsal report and runbook summary.

Can you attach any runbook excerpts or rehearsal reports? Also point us to the contact for SOC2/Security evidence.

We appreciate concise answers we can paste into our scoring spreadsheet (one-line commitment + short clarifier).

-Elena
Elena Martinez
Senior Procurement Manager
Northbridge Financial

Elena / Paul — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise commitments table followed by short clarifications; attaching our runbook excerpt and the multi-region diagram for quick reference. I’ll loop Neha (security) and Grace (SRE/ops) for any technical deep dives.

ONE-LINER COMMITMENTS (for scoring):
- Hosted API (public): automated regional failover; target RTO = 60 minutes (best-effort) for client traffic routing; RPO = approx. 0 for model artifacts, <= 60s for transient inference state under typical load.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): automated failover to designated cold/warm secondary; target RTO = 15 minutes (gold-tier customers with routing pins and cross-region standby); RPO = near-zero for model binaries and config; in-flight KV cache best-effort (up to 30s).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): RTO/RPO depend on customer topology and replication choices; typical guidance: with our recommended warm-standby configuration RTO = 30-120 minutes; RPO configurable to 0 where synchronous replication is deployed.

CLARIFIERS / TECHNICAL DETAILS:
1) Automated vs manual: Hosted API is designed for automated failover by policy (smart routing + cache fallback). Dedicated can be configured for automatic or operator-triggered failover; for the 15-minute commitment we require the customer to adopt our warm-standby template and maintain cross-region capacity reservations. Private deployments vary and are called out in the attached runbook.

2) RPO breakdown:
  - Model artifacts & weights: stored in replicated object store; RPO = 0 for published model versions (we use multi-region replication within our storage backend).
  - Customer data (embeddings, stored conversations): for Hosted API these are written to customer project storage; replication is async by default, typical RPO <= 5 minutes; for Dedicated we offer configurable sync replication (RPO configurable to 0).
  - Inference runtime state (KV cache / in-flight): ephemeral by design — lost state is expected on abrupt failovers. We provide prefix/KV caching best-effort replication where applicable; plan for up to 30–60s of potential context loss unless customer uses explicit session persistence.

3) Failover sequencing & routing:
  - Default path: smart routing in the control plane detects regional health and shifts traffic to a compatible model endpoint in another region; this uses our edge routing with short DNS TTLs plus HTTP-level health checks.
  - DNS TTL: default 60s for Hosted; can be reduced to 10s for Dedicated with BGP/anycast partner options.
  - Alternate (BGP/Anycast): available for Dedicated/Private via partner integration — supports near-instant routing with partner-level cutover.
  - Canary routing: Redwood Console supports gradual traffic split (canary percentage) and automatic rollback based on latency/error metrics.

4) Cross-region durability:
  - Architecture: active-primary with warm-standby replicas (active-passive) for serving runtime; model artifacts stored in strongly-consistent multi-region object store.
  - Replication targets: typical replication lag target for metadata/config is <5s; for large object replication we commit to eventual consistency with monitored replication pipelines; we provide replication metrics and lag thresholds in Console.

5) Testing cadence & evidence:
  - We perform scheduled failover rehearsals quarterly for production clusters; dedicated customers can opt into monthly rehearsals. Attached: Failover rehearsal summary (2026-01-12) and an excerpt of the DR runbook (section: orchestration & operator checklist).

SECURITY / EVIDENCE CONTACT:
- SOC2 and compliance package requests: Neha Kapoor (neha.kapoor@redwood.com). She can provide our latest audit pack and evidence bundle via secure transfer.

ATTACHMENTS: RI-DR-Runbook-v1.4.pdf (runbook excerpt), multi-region-arch-diagram.png (illustration), failover-rehearsal-20260112-report.pdf (recent rehearsal summary).

If you want these distilled to a one-line entry per scoring row I can provide a spreadsheet snippet; otherwise happy to schedule a 30m call with Grace to walk the ops sequence.

—Jonas

Jonas — quick follow-ups from our networking/SRE lead:

1) You mentioned DNS TTL of 60s (Hosted). What is the default DNS provider and can we set a custom TTL per account?
2) For Dedicated customers, do you support BGP announcements or a partner anycast solution we can use to avoid DNS cutover entirely?
3) In the canary scenario, what metrics drive automatic rollback (error rate, tail latency, 5xx spiking)? We need thresholds to map into our runbook.

Also can Neha point us to the SOC2 auditor contact; we may request the auditor statement under NDA.

-Paul

Northbridge Financial

Paul / Elena — answers inline and next steps: 

1) DNS provider & TTL: our global edge uses a mix of managed DNS providers and our edge-layer. Default Hosted TTL = 60s; we can support per-account TTL adjustments down to 10s where necessary. For sub-30s behavior we recommend a combined approach (short TTL + health-aware edge proxy).

2) BGP / Anycast for Dedicated: yes — for Dedicated we support two options:
   - Partner anycast (recommended): works with our network partners to present a single anycast IP; cutover is near-instant and avoids DNS propagation.
   - BGP announcement (customer-run): supported for customers who manage their own prefixes; we provide peering guides and test windows.

3) Canary rollback metrics: Redwood Console will automatically roll back when either:
   - 5xx error rate increases > 0.5 percentage points AND is > 0.1% absolute within the canary window, OR
   - 95th percentile tail latency regresses > 30% vs baseline for the same window.
   These thresholds are default and configurable per rollout. We can supply the exact JSON policy that powers Console rollouts if you want to import it into your orchestration rules.

SOC2 / auditor contact: Neha will coordinate delivery under NDA. Neha — can you send the auditor contact and the secure link to the evidence bundle to Elena?

Next steps proposal: I can prepare a one-page scoring snippet (each row: commitment, scope, evidence link) tomorrow. Grace is available for a 30m technical walkthrough next week (Tue/Wed afternoons PT).

Thanks — Jonas
